A couple of notes on why this is framed this way: multiple pediatric sources note that 
after a seizure, it's normal for a child to be drowsy or confused
, and that this can last 
for up to an hour
. However, guidance also lists ongoing drowsiness, trouble waking, or a child "not acting normally" after a febrile seizure as a trigger to 
seek immediate medical care if... your child is not acting normally... or has trouble staying awake or being woken up
. Given that this can't be assessed remotely and the stakes of missing something serious are high, the safe instruction is to seek emergency evaluation now rather than wait it out at home.
